# FS25 vault capability audit

Status: **in progress**, last updated 14 November 2026. This audit reopens the question that the 65-entry companion validation matrix could not answer: whether every vault mod with useful, distinct data has an honest Farm Dashboard reading. The completed matrix is evidence for its tested integrations, not a vault-wide pass.

## Inventory boundary

- Current read-only `P:\FS25 MOD VAULT\by-category` enumeration: **8,012 ZIP paths**. The maintained vault index dated 26 October lists 8,011, so it is not an exact current inventory.
- A 14 November read-only filesystem count still found 8,012 ZIP paths. It did not rerun the Lua/content scan; unchanged path count alone does not prove unchanged archive bytes or preserve the 1,803 Lua-bearing classification.
- The 23 September source-screening inventory covered **665 ZIP names**. By filename, 602 remain in the current category tree, 63 are absent, and 7,407 distinct current names were outside that older sample. Filename overlap is a triage aid, not proof of identical bytes or versions.
- The read-only `2026-10-31-scan-vault.py` scan covered all 8,012 current category-tree ZIP paths. **1,803** contain Lua and **1,549** declare source files in `modDesc.xml`. **1,201** Lua-bearing ZIP names were outside the older 665-name screen. The full machine-readable result is `Z:\Graham\agent-comms\farmhub-companion-acceptance\VAULT-SCAN-2026-10-31.json`.
- `FS25_Bale_Storage.zip` in `uncategorized` was unreadable as a ZIP; its contents and playability are unproved. No vault files were modified.
- A title/category/source-file keyword pass put **118 ZIPs across 91 normalized titles** into an initial review queue. The queue includes duplicate versions, RF packages, native-data overlap and false positives; **118 is not a missing-integration count**. The sortable 1,201-row Lua triage file is `Z:\Graham\agent-comms\farmhub-companion-acceptance\VAULT-LUA-TRIAGE-2026-10-31.csv`. Every row is still a source-review lead, not an acceptance result. Lower-scoring rows must also be assessed before claiming the vault audit exhaustive.
- The repeatable `2026-11-08-vault-review-queue.py` compares exact archive names in the 7 November 1,803-row Lua-signal snapshot with this audit and prints current counts at configurable score thresholds. Its optional `--group` view puts absent names under their title/version for triage and flags when the title occurs in this audit. On 13 November, the score-7-or-higher queue had 627 eligible rows and **zero exact archive names absent** after the recent source classifications. This is a **name-mention check only**, not 627 source reviews, a missing-integration count, duplicate-byte proof, installed acceptance or an exhaustive vault audit. Maps, RF-owned packages, duplicate versions and control-only mods appear in the queue; lower-score candidates and source-backed open gaps still require work. The check chooses the next review without treating a textual mention as acceptance.

The current 13 November R4 name check has **zero absent archive names among 1,801 score-0-or-higher eligible paths**, including 1,575 at score 1 or above. The last 120 score-zero names were brought into the audit or linked exact-path registers below; two root-declared encoded Ursus scripts remain **OPEN**, while a third copy has no declared root load path. These are scanner/name-coverage figures, not 1,801 full source reviews, a count of missing integrations, installed acceptance, or proof that every vault ZIP has been screened for farm value. The two remaining Lua-bearing signal rows scored -2 and were separately source-classified on 14 November below. The five score-1 archives with combined apparent farm/outcome or persistence/outcome word signals were inspected in the residual writer check below; those word hits did not establish an additional usable farm ledger. Rerun the count after any scan or audit change.

## Current Ally compatibility boundary, 14 November

The V61/V68 `DLC_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED:1.2.1.0` StockGuard refusals below are historical results from those exact runs. Tina's later V90R1 disposable run used the current as-found selected set plus Farm Dashboard and Hand Tool Drop; its retained `Z:\Graham\agent-comms\ally-fh-vault-v90r1-evidence\game-log-live.txt` records `Load dlc: pdlc_pumpsAndHosesPack` (line 689), StockGuard load (line 851) and `capacity: READY` with 243 fill types / 61 ground types (line 2769). The V90R1 result separately reports one installed V5 Windows row, committed exports and full fresh-baseline restoration. Thus the old DLC-version refusal is **not a current global Ally blocker** for that bounded selected set. It does not establish that Manual Attach, Production Advisor, other source-tested candidates or all 488 listed mods coexist with StockGuard. Each candidate still needs its own selected-mod load and nonempty game/export/installed-page evidence. Older paragraphs saying testing is "currently blocked" describe their earlier evidence point, not a fresh 14 November refusal.

## Decision rule

For each candidate, establish the exact current ZIP hash/version and source-owned state. Before adding a collector or page, name the practical farm question it answers and the action the farmer can take from the reading; require that the value is distinct from the normal game export, correctly scoped and safely readable. A saved field, placeable or setting alone is not a reason to add UI. Where a useful reading is justified, compare a fresh nonempty game state, committed export and installed page. Classify native-game overlap and detection-only mods honestly. Never call an empty, unavailable or settings-only result a gameplay pass. RF-owned Ally work has priority. Graham authorised bounded PC testing on 13 November until he returns; the PC must still be checked and backed up before any live change. No public release, main push or RF/VPS changes are in scope.

The value gate also applies to test fixtures: placing a building merely to make a collector nonempty does not establish that Graham needs the reading. Before any future fixture or page, record the specific decision it supports, whether the game already shows the same answer, whose land or asset the reading belongs to, and whether the result is an observed state or an estimate. A source-only page remains unaccepted until its nonempty case and ownership are proved. Do not alter Graham's active save to manufacture that case. Graham reiterated on 13 November that collecting and showing a value needs an actual farming use: do not place buildings, buy equipment or create stock merely to generate dashboard rows. A candidate for an owned asset is conditional on the farm actually owning it and on a useful action from its reading.

Future Ally packets must check available installer space before staging and stop BLOCKED if it is insufficient. A FarmHub test does not authorize deletion of any pre-existing backup, log or unrelated file to make space; any proposed cleanup needs separate provenance and byte-preservation review first. The V85R1 `bk523`/`bk526` loss remains an exception, not a precedent.

Its `lastLowered` and held-input state are runtime control state, with no mod-owned save ledger in the reviewed Lua. - Multiplayer Achievements - Per Player v1.0.0.0 (`gameplay/FS25_374265_Multiplayer_Achievements_-_Per_Player.zip`, SHA-256 `7FD0AE6E0EC4D163B890D60C1C6B128032481FBA1F022113634A1EE372BF5F89`) has two different scopes. `modSettings/FS25_MultiplayerAchievements/progress.xml` is **personal profile** progress and must not be exported as a farm reading. Separately, `MPAchievementShared` stores a `mpaLedger` on each `Farm` in the save XML: eligible clean-money balance/peak and cow, sheep, pig and chicken breeding counts. Its hooks and snapshots run only when the mission is multiplayer, game-started and server-owned. This is a genuine farm-keyed candidate distinct from the current bank balance, because the mod deliberately excludes cheat/unsupported income and ineligible breeding. A source-tested read-only collector/page now require active, game-started server multiplayer, exact export farm and an existing ledger; they read the fields without calling `getLedger` (which initializes/clamps state), apply its non-mutating balance clamp and label values as eligibility counters rather than bank balance or realized profit. Focused exact-farm, foreign-farm, malformed-ledger, single-player/client and UI tests passed, as did typecheck and Vite build. No nonempty multiplayer game/export/installed proof or private package exists yet; a single-player Ally save cannot validate this path, and Ally is currently blocked at StockGuard's DLC-version gate.

Native-overlap examples need a different decision: `Statistics Extended` v1.0.0.1 (`FS25_364343_FS25_statsExtended.zip`, SHA-256 `EE6C655FE2E61D2DC0A19B14884AC316C802F106C1729D85A31095BA2450643C`) reads `farm.stats.statistics` session and total counters and `farm.stats:getTotalValue()` achievement progress for the local farm when its in-game tab opens. Its five Lua files have no savegame XML writer or new counter accumulator; the package is a presentation of native statistics, not a distinct mod-owned ledger. `Animal Storage Overview` reads standard husbandry storage/food values to extend the in-game Animals frame. Those can motivate better generic Farm Dashboard views, but their source does not yet establish unique mod-owned state requiring an optional collector. `Ingame Time Operating Hours` changes the game's effective hour/fuel behaviour; avoid counting a second copy of native hours as a new mod-specific metric.

Two high-ranked vault leads are **already source-integrated but lack a meaningful nonempty installed pass**. Field Profitability Ledger v1.0.1.0 (`FS25_369866_FS25_FieldProfitabilityLedger.zip`, SHA-256 `F4A832326835C42D4454376250D6997427C6635A1F7030432684AB0342D80B32`) exposes its single-player `Runtime.SinglePlayerRuntime.listCycles({farmId=...})` and `queryCycle` methods. The historical B2 matrix marked its reader unavailable, so a nonempty field-cycle game/export/UI comparison is still needed. The uncategorized `KM_80685_Field_Profitability_Ledger.zip` is byte-identical; the GitHub-named v1.0.0.0 archive is an older distinct version. Farmland Marketplace v1.0.5.0 (`FS25_369241_FS25_FarmlandMarketplace.zip`, SHA-256 `331588DE99894BB62FB8EC5D43B28F8B29C64CE6674C204E6A6C4C943DAF7DB1`) exposes `FlaechenVermarktung.manager.state` with sale offers, lease offers and leases. FarmHub already filters those rows to offers/contracts touching the export farm, but B2 reported unavailable; a live offer or lease on a disposable save is needed before claiming meaningful value. These are acceptance gaps, not new missing adapters.

## Production Booster System source lead

The exact vault `KM_82331_Production_Booster_System.zip` is v1.0.0.0, SHA-256 `58D1267C5396C483DC524F43EAE9818C21C7129864CAE3A989C255706F04214C`. It also saves input priorities and manual booster-enable choices. These are distinct mod-tracked figures, beyond a native current fill level. The source updates the output counters when an owned production runs; they are not sales, deliveries or realized profit. Static XML booster configuration is not a player's saved choice.

A first read-only collector and full page now take only server statistics for the export farm's currently owned points and list nonzero output-by-fill-type base, actual and extra litres. It deliberately omits aggregate output across different fill types, costs, priority settings and booster consumption from this first view. Focused source-shape tests cover a nonempty owned line, foreign exclusion and client-only withholding. **This is source-tested only**: no game run, positive production, committed export or installed-page comparison exists. Production Booster System's coexistence with the normal RF-owned StockGuard set is unproved; the Production Control refusal does not establish this mod's outcome. A meaningful installed test needs a disposable owned production that runs with the exact mod, a nonzero recorded output and matching game/mod statistic, export and installed page.

## Vehicle Trade In source lead

Vehicle Trade In v1.0.0.1 (`FS25_362333_FS25_TradeInMenu.zip` and `objects/KM_79798_Vehicle_Trade_In.zip` are byte-identical, SHA-256 `CD8F6BD2189328595536A4BAA2F62FB81F235611437134C310800DA41F01C310`) has a mod-owned `tradeInStatistics.xml` ledger. The exact `TradeInStatistics.lua` retains up to 200 completed dealer transactions, each with farm ID, vehicle name, base appraisal, final trade credit and date; `scripts/main.lua` attaches the runtime as `mission.tradeInMod`, and the mod's Statistics GUI reads that runtime. Completed trade credit is distinct from native current vehicle value. The used-market offer list is shared market state, and financing agreements have separate binding/payment rules; neither is copied by this first reader. A `main.lua` comment says 1.1.0.0, but the packaged `modDesc.xml` declares **1.0.0.1**.

The exact `serverFinalizeTrade` path records a history row only **after** a replacement-vehicle purchase succeeds and the old vehicle is removed. Starting a trade or viewing its appraisal does not create an accepted ledger row; cancelling refunds the temporary credit. A nonempty installed acceptance therefore needs one bounded, completed trade on a disposable unsaved save, with the original vehicle, replacement and credit clearly identified before confirmation. Do not infer completed history from a pending transaction or native vehicle sale.

A read-only collector and full page now take only the exact export farm's completed transaction rows from the server runtime and label the final value as trade credit, not profit. The mod's XML loader substitutes farm 1 for a legacy row with no farm ID before the dashboard can inspect its origin, so the reader withholds farm 1 history in multiplayer rather than risk misattribution. It also withholds client-only or unbound registers and never invokes the mod's mutating save/reset paths. Two focused tests cover nonempty farm isolation, base-appraisal versus final-credit values, no mutation and the multiplayer legacy-owner gate; TypeScript typecheck, Vite build and existing 27-locale verification passed. English fallback copy has 13 new labels. This is **source-tested only**. No completed game trade, same-generation export, installed page, finance payoff, or multiplayer acceptance exists. A future bounded test would require an explicitly approved disposable trade and exact before/after value comparison; an empty ledger alone would not prove value.

FarmHub's first reader recreates only the mod's key for live husbandries whose `getOwnerFarmId()` exactly matches the export farm. It exports named pen/animal and sick counts plus the disease category when sick, omitting animal names and treatment detail. Missing owned-pen state is marked partial; a client-only snapshot is withheld. Two focused Lua/merge tests, TypeScript typecheck, Vite build and existing locale verification passed. This is **source-tested only**: no positive illness, game treatment, nonempty installed page, multiplayer or save/load proof exists. A healthy zero in a pen is not a treatment pass.

The exact `FS25_MarketDynamics.zip` v1.3.1.43 (SHA-256 `D59ADC02B073E399920F1748297B1667A5D6B65046E81DFAF658A99ABF774051`) is RF-owned. No installed multi-farm futures acceptance exists, and RF source was not changed. Market-wide events and price movers remain save-wide context rather than farm-owned contract rows.

- FarmKit v1.0.0.3 (`gameplay/GH_NXModdingFS__FS25_FarmKit_FS25_FarmKit.zip`, SHA-256 `64EEABA4BF5D29E72B5205AAF5997D1E9830F61D460098488E150A998974A745`) is one high-ranked field-planning candidate. Its server builds `fieldEntryServerCache` entries keyed by field ID, each with a farm ID, area, fertilizer/lime/herbicide/material rates and total litres; its seed dialog calculates per-crop litres from field area and seed rate. With Precision Farming active it reads live soil/pH/nitrogen/cover maps; without it, the vanilla entry uses spray-type rates and area. These figures are **derived current estimates**, not a persisted record of application or purchases. The separately saved organic-nitrogen mode is save-wide, and the many feature toggles are profile settings rather than farm-owned outcomes. Farm Dashboard already shows field need flags but does not expose this mod's per-material litre planning table. A useful bounded reader would consume only an already populated server cache, require exact current field ownership, label the figures as estimates and record cache freshness/mode; it must not call `getFieldEntriesForNetwork`, which refreshes the cache. Exact source shows the server cache is warmed once per field on update, while later cache refreshes depend on network requests; a cached entry may be stale. The mod's `getFarmIdForField` falls back to the current player farm when a farmland owner is unavailable, so a reader must independently verify the live farmland owner and never trust that fallback for farm isolation. No collector, game/export/page comparison, PF-mode validation or installed acceptance exists yet.

  **13 November freshness gate:** the exact ZIP rehashed to the stated SHA-256. `NXFarmKit.lua` sets a five-second TTL only on `fieldEntryNetworkCache`; `fieldEntryServerCache` has no timestamp or expiry. Warmup processes one field per update, then marks itself finished. `getFieldEntriesForNetwork` refreshes every field's server-cache fingerprint, but calling it from FarmHub would run the mod's rebuild path and violate the passive-reader boundary. The entry's own farm ID can also fall back to the current player when ownership lookup fails. A passive exporter cannot prove that a stored estimate still matches current field/PF conditions from the cache fields alone. No dashboard litre recommendation should be added from this cache until a bounded, nonmutating freshness check and independent land-owner join are demonstrated. No field work, purchase or cache refresh was triggered for this source review.

- Field To-Do List exact source check adds a stricter migration boundary to the earlier candidate note. `ToDoManager:loadFromXMLFile` calls `migrateOrphanTaskFarmIds()`, which assigns every legacy task missing `farmId` to the then-local farm in memory; `taskBelongsToFarm(task, farmId)` also returns true for a nil task farm ID. Therefore filtering the **live** `manualTasks` table by numeric `farmId` alone cannot prove historical ownership after load. A safe multi-farm reading needs original saved-row provenance (or a source migration contract that identifies legacy rows), plus current field ownership for planned crops; creating a normal manual task in a disposable save would test only new-task handling. The task collector remains deferred. The separate planned-crop collector rechecks current farmland ownership, while explicitly leaving plan authorship unproved.

  **Migration provenance follow-up (14 November, exact source):** Rehashed the reviewed ZIP to `D1B428B296F93906AD8A297E07726F3FE7F70C1828452909791B0B8CF798BE18`. `ToDoManager:loadFromXMLFile` calls `migrateOrphanTaskFarmIds` after loading each task (lines 1992-2009). `saveToSavegameDirectory` calls that migration again before writing (line 2156), and `saveTaskToXML` emits `#farmId` for every assigned task (lines 2051-60). Thus a **later saved XML with an explicit farm ID is not sufficient provenance**: it can contain a legacy task assigned solely by the migration. Matching live task IDs to that later file cannot distinguish those tasks from genuinely farm-authored ones. A safe historical multi-farm task reading would require a pre-migration source/contract or other independently proved lineage; a new task created during a disposable test proves only the new-task path. No task collector or installed task claim was added.

- PTO Load System v1.0.0.0 (`gameplay/FS25_372063_PTO_Load_System.zip`, SHA-256 `4AAEFA588D11BD2817E491F3FAF366A20C8DF534FB0F722D740931EDD44E64FF`) has a **distinct transient calculation lead**, not a saved power or work ledger. 2026-11-14 exact-source follow-up: the reviewed ZIP was rehashed. `AttachPowerTakeOffsManually.lua` and `AttachConnectionHosesManually.lua` initialise empty maps on vehicle load, key live connection flags by `jointDescIndex`, and save a boolean for **each attached implement** together with its unique ID and input joint index (PTO lines 81-86, 129-145; hoses lines 85-90, 120-136). An empty map entry alone does not mean a missing required connection: the action UI first tests whether the paired implement actually has input PTO or hose connectors, and some connections auto-attach or are controlled from inside (PTO lines 389-425; hoses lines 400-450). The game's local action prompt already reports attach/detach availability at the equipment. A FarmHub export on a large fleet can lag a live joint change by an adaptive collection cycle (the observed 143-vehicle V83R2 game used a 120-second cycle), making a dashboard readiness warning potentially stale. **Decision: defer a dedicated page** until an observed use case needs a remote current-state snapshot, the same joint's eligibility and both endpoints can be proved, and freshness can be shown. This mod has distinct data, but no useful, safely timed FarmHub metric has yet been established. No game or installed compatibility test was made for it.

2026-11-14 overlap correction: FarmHub already has a source-tested `manualAttach` owned-implement connection page for the **different** `FS25_340627_FS25_manualAttach` v1.1.0.0 ZIP (see its entry below). Both mods answer the same practical question: whether a hitched implement needs its PTO or hoses connected. The existing collector reads that mod's `PowerTakeOffExtension` and `ConnectionHosesExtension` methods on the implement. `FS25_340665_Attach_Implements_Manually` instead keeps `attachedPTOs[jointDescIndex]` and `attachedHoses[jointDescIndex]` on the **parent attacher** and uses paired joint eligibility helpers. Simply adding its name to the existing detector would falsely imply support; a second, exact-version adapter would need to match the currently attached implement, parent joint and both owners, and handle auto-connection/load-pending cases. Even that adapter would feed the **existing** readiness view, not justify another page. Neither mod's connection page has nonempty game/export/installed acceptance; the second mod remains source-classified only. This narrows the earlier "distinct live state" wording to a distinct implementation of an already identified user need, not an additional integration count.

Later 14 November product decision supersedes that readiness-view proposal for **both** Manual Attach implementations: Graham found no practical dashboard action from remote PTO/hose status and requested only a base-game attached-equipment line on tractors. The `FS25_340627` page was removed in `de2966fe`; no adapter will be added for `FS25_340665` on the reviewed value case. Both exact source implementations remain documented as distinct, but neither is a missing approved FarmHub capability. The base-game line reports direct attached equipment names and does **not** claim hose/PTO connection state.

- Storage Warnings (`objects/KM_81400_storage-warnings-storage-and-warehouse-control.zip`, SHA-256 `D942FFA8B02BFA6F55E15F18AE1B68138E8F9BBD879753FA34385E806F861A2B`) is a **derived live-alert candidate**, not a new storage ledger. Its `modDesc.xml` declares v1.0.1.0 while the Lua `SW.VERSION` constant says 1.6.0.1, so identify the integration by exact bytes. `StorageWarnings.alerts` holds sorted construction, animal, production and storage warning rows with severity, percent, object/fill names and optional quantities. `scan()` rebuilds them from current native farm-owned objects, sets `lastScanStats.farmId`, and `update()` runs it only with a local player while the mod is enabled and settings panel closed. Its thresholds and category switches persist in the local profile's `modSettings/FS25_StorageWarnings.xml`; no alert history is saved. A reader could copy only an already computed snapshot whose `lastScanStats.farmId` equals the selected farm, label it as a local-player current alert snapshot, and withhold stale/remote-client state; it must not invoke `scan()` or imply the alerts are durable events. **Dedicated-server boundary:** `SW:update` returns before `scan()` whenever `g_localPlayer` is nil, so a server exporter cannot rely on a refreshed alert list there despite the descriptor's multiplayer flag. Its `loadMap` clears both the alerts and scan stats. Adding a general FarmHub page now would mostly duplicate native condition data while leaving the dedicated-server case unavailable. Defer a page until a live host/local snapshot can be demonstrated as meaningful and a separate server-safe data contract exists; no collector or installed game/export/page comparison has been made.

## 2026-11-07 Ritter Fresh source lead

`gameplay/GH_rittermod__FS25_Fresh_FS25_Fresh.zip` declares v1.1.0.0-dev.1 and hashes to SHA-256 `C2182676DADAE4CA20926614F143C9EE13A8E5244A5088182452A108F64E20EF`. It has distinct save-local freshness batches and a loss log, beyond native Storage levels. `RmLossTracker:recordExpiration` runs on the server and writes a loss row with amount, fill type, game date, location, entity type, storage class and `farmId`; `RmFreshIO:saveLog` persists that row in `rm_FreshLog.xml` and `loadLog` restores it. The row's `value` is calculated at expiration from fill-type base price, seasonal factor and economy multiplier. It is an **estimated market value of expired goods**, not a recorded sale, debit or realized expense. The source starts with `container.farmId` and checks a live entity owner only when the container farm ID is zero, so an exact-farm filter can show the mod-recorded farm ID but cannot independently prove historical ownership or detect a stale nonzero owner. The global `statistics.totalExpired` is not farm-keyed and must not be presented as a farm total. Current container freshness needs a separate live-owner/reconciliation check before it can be shown as current farm stock.

Farm Dashboard now has a **source-tested read-only candidate** for the exact version: a detected Storage companion page scans no more than the newest 2,000 log entries, shows at most 40 valid rows for the selected farm, and labels counts/litres as the scanned window. It withholds ownerless/foreign rows, invalid dates/amounts, client-only state and an unready manager; a source `value` of zero is shown as an unavailable estimate. It never calls the mod's expiration, loading or aggregation methods. Five focused Lua/merge/UI tests, 17 catalog/presentation tests, UI typecheck and Vite build passed. No private package, nonempty game/export/installed-page comparison or expiration gameplay has been accepted. Ally normal-set loading remains blocked by RF StockGuard's DLC-version refusal.

**Current freshness needs a live ownership check:** The same exact ZIP exposes `RmFreshManager:getInventorySummary(farmId)` and `getExpiringWithin(hours, farmId)`, but both select current containers by the cached `container.farmId`. On save reconciliation, `registerContainer` replaces the identity and attaches `runtimeEntity` without refreshing that farm ID. A vehicle, bale or placeable could have changed owner after the cached value was recorded; the summary alone cannot prove present ownership. Object-storage entries use an abstract stored object as `runtimeEntity`, with the storage placeable's owner copied into metadata at registration. Farm Dashboard now has a **source-tested candidate** in the existing Ritter Fresh page: it resolves a normal container's current runtime owner, or matches an abstract object to the current owning storage placeable by unique ID and object reference, before including any batch. Unresolved owners are withheld and coverage is partial; the page distinguishes Ritter Fresh batch amounts from independently measured native Storage levels and labels expiry-disabled state. A focused stale-owner/stored-object Lua test, UI test, typecheck and Vite build pass. The existing loss log remains a historical mod-recorded farm attribution. No nonempty game/export/installed-page proof, live transfer test or private package is claimed, and normal-set Ally loading is still blocked by RF StockGuard's DLC-version refusal.

Its `CHO.orders` contains useful accepted-order requirements, progress, deadline and reward, but each order has no farm ID. The action event transmits a `farmId` that `respondToOrder` does not bind to the accepted order; the server broadcasts the common order queue. A delivered bale's owner can determine the **payment farm** at completion, which does not retroactively identify the owner of every pending order. - **Bank And Credit is a distinct farm-keyed loan register:** Exact `objects/KM_77828_Bank_And_Credit.zip` v1.1.0.0 hashes to SHA-256 `EF48ABBF420C06824CCF729F33079BA95273A6B0E40397A6D57DD4B1D7AAB6A2`. Its `BankRepository` persists `bankCredit.xml`; every `Loan` has a farm ID, type (annuity, bullet or revolving), original and remaining principal, interest rate, remaining duration, monthly payment and paid-off state. The source binds the repository at `g_currentMission.bankManager.repository` and exposes `getByFarm(farmId)`. `restAmount` means outstanding principal for annuity/bullet and drawn amount for revolving; `amount` is the original principal or revolving limit. FarmHub now has a **source-tested read-only candidate** for exact v1.1.0.0. The saved XML attribute or signature alone cannot recover original farm-1 ownership. Farm IDs above 1 remain distinguishable from this fallback, but a page that works only for those farms would leave the normal farm-1 path unproved. No general selected-farm collector should be added until the third-party source supplies explicit ownership provenance or a separately verified safe join; a controlled new-order fixture could prove only that fixture. ## 2026-11-08 Use Your Tyres source-tested page

The exact v1.1.0.0 bytes above increment each supported wheel's `uytTravelledDist` on ground/object contact, restore the current wheel configuration on load, and calculate wear from travel, wheel perimeter, the 240,000 m base and the current global distance multiplier. The in-game HUD reports the highest wheel wear, so FarmHub presents each current wheel's recorded travel (km) and calculated wear, plus the farm's highest calculated wear. The Dashboard does not use the save hook or read inactive wheel configurations; the live wheel distance is the export source. Current vehicle ownership and server state are rechecked, the version is pinned, malformed or duplicate readings withhold farm totals, and rows are bounded. A zero reading can mean a newly tracked or replaced wheel; it is not a replacement event. Wheel travel is not the same as vehicle odometer mileage.

The dedicated Lua collector, Companion Mods detection and NEW APP page are source-tested with farm-filtering, multiplier, zero-wheel, duplicate/malformed, version and client gates. Focused Lua/merge/UI tests, TypeScript typecheck, Vite build, descriptor parse and 15 keys in all 27 locales passed. There is no private package, nonempty game/committed-export/installed-page comparison, tyre replacement, or normal-set coexistence with Real Tire Wear/AutoSwitch/StockGuard.

A reader must decode the cell centre, resolve its current farmland ID and owner with the engine's `FarmlandManager:getFarmlandIdAtWorldPosition` / `getFarmlandOwner`, and exclude unknown or foreign land. The 1 m grid can hold very many cells, so a full scan inside a single export tick is unsafe; a bounded incremental aggregation and explicit incomplete-state contract are needed before a page can claim per-farm prepared area or bonus bands. Ownership at read time does not prove which farm performed the work, and prepared cells can cross field boundaries. The local FS25 1.20 extract and LUADOC confirm the farmland query methods; no installed version-1.25 spatial performance or nonempty game/export/page result is established. ## 2026-11-08 V67R1 Production Schedule result and reader fix

Tina returned `PARTIAL FARMHUB-ALLY-20261108-VAULT-V67R1` at 14:57 UTC with full Ally restoration. The frozen packet, V5 5.2.88 installer, exporter 5.1.0.75 and exact Production Schedule ZIP rehash to `7F73E8A4…EDDC7C6`, `598B2D1D…278CB`, `33E5803F…E37B` and `1E5C945C…CC146` respectively. The game screenshot shows the owned Small Glass Greenhouse Chili Peppers schedule active after one Q status toggle from the world-view dialog. The mod wrote `productionSchedule.xml` for the same greenhouse key with `production id="chilli" status="aktiv"`. No month was toggled, so calendar index mapping and period enforcement remain unproved.

The marker-selected q5 slot b is publication sequence 10, generation 9, sourceSlot savegame20; its base64 payload has declared and actual length 1,044,170 bytes, matching Adler-32 `1927483414`, and parses to the preserved decoded JSON. Native production lists the farm-1 greenhouse with seven recipes; the Production Schedule adapter still reports `readState=unavailable`, `reason=no-owned-production-list`. The installed 5.2.88 card shows the same unavailable state while Factory Profit Calculator renders that greenhouse. Tina's readback reports one Windows row during the run, no schedule/FarmDash Lua stack, 484 original mods and 517 modSettings hash-restored, disposable slot20 removed, and 18 real-save slots/1,656 files unchanged. This is a game-side schedule save with a **failed FarmHub read**, not an integrated-value PASS.

Source diagnosis found that this collector alone fetched `g_currentMission` with `rawget(_G, "g_currentMission")`. The FarmHub Lua environment inherits engine globals through `__index`, so the raw lookup misses the live mission and necessarily leaves the production manager unavailable. Other production readers use `_G.g_currentMission`. The source fix uses inherited lookup, and the focused Fengari test now covers both direct and inherited mission environments. The fix remains **source-tested only** until an installed retest shows the active Chili Peppers row in a later committed generation. No normal StockGuard coexistence or public release claim follows.

The corrected exporter 5.1.0.76 was privately packaged with SHA-256 `0D64FE24E742638CE3CA4692C2660D2E67CF11F7C64081E9EF4B1165E4A12043`; its 246 archive entries have unique safe paths, pass CRC, and the descriptor/runtime/collector bytes match source. V5 UI is unchanged, so the existing 5.2.88 installer `598B2D1D…278CB` is reused. A focused test also distinguishes absent mission, absent production API and failed list calls if the reading remains unavailable. Frozen `TEST-PACKET-V67R2.md` SHA-256 `19F936E0383107596B07602B00FC35AA1FB8CEB214F55B2B21BC3251DA390E69` was queued only after V67R1 full restoration and an RF ownership check. Tina's ACK, if received, is receipt only; the installed fix remains unproved.

- Trip Computer v1.0.0.0 `FS25_341715_Trip_Computer.zip` SHA-256 `D368CEB5A0DF79995D5A7475350134EFFB5770930B10DFEBE13CD8A41AE86BED` adds `spec_tripComputer` to motorized vehicles but uses it only where a fuel system exists. Its server update accumulates driven distance in metres, estimated fuel consumption in litres and motor-on time in milliseconds. It defines a `saveToXMLFile` method and a matching reload conversion from seconds to milliseconds. The local FS25 1.20 `Vehicle:saveToXMLFile` directly calls `spec.saveToXMLFile` for each specialization with that method; a separate registered save event is **not required**. That establishes a source-backed save path, while actual save/reload persistence remains untested. A reset from a distance/fuel mode clears all three counters, while the operating-time display mode itself refuses reset. This is a distinct live resettable trip record, not the lifetime Vehicle Mileage reading. It overlaps HUD+ resettable distance/fuel, so the two should never be added together. The read-only `tripComputer` collector/page reports per-owned-vehicle kilometres, litres and hours from those in-memory values, with no combined farm sum because each trip may have been reset at a different time. Focused source/merge and UI checks are recorded with the commit. The exact mod was not run at that stage; a nonzero same-vehicle game/export/installed comparison, reset behavior and save/reload persistence were untested. Fuel used here is the mod's estimate, not a purchase or expense.

- The read-only `autoSwitchRegister` collector/page is **source-tested only** for this exact AutoSwitch version. A 14 November exact-source correction withholds its sale rows: base `SellingStation:sellFillType` returns **price**, whereas `scripts/Register.lua` passes the overwritten function's return to `addSale` as **litres**, then derives kilograms from that value. This makes the register's sale quantity unreliable even when an event is genuine; neither the UI nor exporter should present it as delivered volume. The current collector reads only live server weighings, filters by export farm, validates dates and kilograms, shows recent records, withholds totals on invalid or truncated state, and never calls mutating methods. Empty arrays do not assert a zero-valued farm history because the source has no reliable loaded flag. Four focused Lua collector cases and one rendered-page case pass for the corrected shape. The earlier source test, TypeScript build and locale verification predated this correction; new checks are recorded below. No nonempty game weighing, committed export, installed-page parity, AutoDrive weighbridge run or normal-set coexistence has been accepted.

- Test Drive `uncategorized/FS25_326754_Test_Drive.zip` v1.0.0.0 SHA-256 `BA4F9D7F78FA355EE894B1B5386EF53D8B6283F65848E9340095CDCA0D5FFE8A` offers a temporary leased shop vehicle and charges insurance through native `LEASING_COSTS`. Its vehicle save hook writes an `isTestDrive` flag and remaining timer, but the exact `Vehicle.load` hook sets `isTestDriveVehicle = false` immediately after its conditional timer restart. This is a third-party source concern; a resumed active test drive cannot be inferred from the saved flag without game proof. The mod has no durable trial history, decision score or separate expense ledger. No test drive, insurance payment or save/reload was performed.

A current parameter can also reflect other mods; neither it nor a multiplier is an owned-field forecast or measured harvest. Three focused Lua/merge tests, TypeScript typecheck, Vite build, descriptor parse and locale coverage pass. **Source-tested only**: no private package, installed game/export/page comparison, nondefault in-game setting or coexistence test yet.

A new read-only collector/page gates the exact mod/version, server and current farm, reads CVT-enabled settings from currently owned vehicles, maps the source's load-limit steps to 0–20%, and withholds counts on malformed or truncated states. It does not claim measured power, fuel use, wear, fieldwork, or persistence after a real reload. Three focused Lua/merge tests, typecheck and descriptor parse passed; packaging and installed nonempty game/export/page acceptance remain pending.
- Teach-IN Extension `FS25_359573_Teach-IN_Extension.zip` v1.0.0.0 SHA-256 `E7175080E320E5E7F634BE08C539AF922E2911461A2F64C25167A541E2E36ED8` stores editable four-tab sequences and ten profiles in the **single profile-wide** `modSettings/FS25_TeachIN/FS25_TeachIN.xml` path. Despite the `getSavegamePath` method name, that path does not include the save slot or a farm ID. The vehicle specialization handles inputs but the reviewed source does not attach those profiles to an owned vehicle. A headless farm export cannot attribute profile steps to the current farm/save without additional binding; no separate farm page or sequence-execution claim is made.

Wood Manager and Grape And Olive Yield Settings pages were later removed under the value rule; their detectors remain. The original catalog parity and alias tests passed in source. Discovery wiring does not establish installed runtime acceptance for the remaining pages.

Until that natural fixture exists, this remains a source-only conditional capability, not an accepted farming benefit.

## 2026-11-13 independent Ally deadline probe

V76R1's hidden watchdog logged ARMED but disappeared before its deadline while the disposable game remained live; Tina could not recover its exact launch command or exit cause. The separate source-only `tools/ally-disposable-game-scheduled-deadline.ps1` uses an exact FS25 PID/start pair and a one-shot Task Scheduler action, but registration source and an ARMED line are not proof that a scheduled action fires after the launching shell exits. ### Current page value gate (13 November)

For a dedicated page, the reader must answer a named farm decision or report a useful observed result. A mod being loadable, a value being nondefault, a UI control being readable, or a source fixture being nonempty is insufficient by itself. Do not place a building, buy a machine or alter a save merely to populate a page. Detection can remain in the catalog without a dedicated collector or page. Keep source testing, private packaging and game/export/installed acceptance separate.

- **Retain a planning or readiness reading when it has a concrete input:** Animal Food Calculator's owned-pen feed/water estimates can guide supply planning, but an uncached pen must remain uncalculated; Adjust Production Points compares a farm-owned production point's current recipe rates and capacities with its baseline or saved values, which can expose a planning difference; Capacity Upgrade reports the current usable tank capacity on an owned vehicle; Automatic Loan Repay combines the farm's loan and balance with the armed schedule to project the next repayment. These source semantics justify the pages, but do not expand their existing installed-acceptance claims.
- **Keep a source question open where the page is policy-only:** Resource Usage Control has one accepted nondefault save-wide multiplier display, but the page does not itself calculate seed/spray quantities or spending for any field. Crop Control Override has one accepted changed WHEAT rule display, but no observed field replanning or planting restriction. Their prior bounded comparisons remain valid as policy-display evidence. Neither should be presented as measured farm usage or field outcome; a future value improvement must connect policy to an actual planning question or observed effect before claiming the broader integration complete.
- **Retain event/location readers separately from switch pages:** Flock Camera has an owned-placeable event list, and Hand Tool Drop can report an owned dropped tool's actual position. These are distinct from camera LED preferences and Hand Tools mode switches; their value depends on real nonempty, attributable event/location evidence, not an invented fixture.

A source inventory at this point found ten full pages with neither `farmData` nor `farmId` in the renderer: Animal Food Overview (feed recipe reference), Crop Control Override (save-wide policy), Dynamic Market, Fluctuating Diesel Price, Market Price Helper and Realistic Diesel Price (market price or price-history readings), Imperial System (display units), Regional Crop Calendar (plant/harvest planning windows), Resource Usage Control (save-wide policy), and Smart Crop Control (named NPC field plan). Resource Usage Control was subsequently removed as described below, leaving nine from that inventory. Crop Control Override remains a policy reading with a direct planting-eligibility decision; the other eight have stated planning/reference uses, but page source alone does not upgrade any runtime acceptance. This inventory does not prove all other pages are valuable or accepted.

Dynamic Market's source page had a market-outlook explanation but did not explicitly distinguish shared prices from the selected farm's sales or income. Its lead now labels the shared market scope and names the actual decision: when and where to sell. This is a wording correction to the current source, not fresh station-pressure gameplay, sales or installed-page acceptance.

### Restricted Periods existing-page version correction (13 November)

The earlier conditional-lead paragraph did not reflect that the V5 source already had a Restricted Periods full page and an overview reading. Review of exact `FS25_352961_Restricted_Periods.zip` v1.0.0.0 above confirmed the period/frost rules and that `getVehicleBanCategory` checks a vehicle's selected fill type. The pre-existing page's static twelve-period grid could render for a different or unknown installed version, while its core overview labelled the window as the reviewed 1.0.0.0 rules without checking the active mod's version. This could present an unreviewed rule as operational advice. Current source now gates both exporters on the active mod's exact `1.0.0.0` descriptor version and withholds live tiles and the rule grid in the page for a different/unknown version. Focused Lua producer, full-page, merge, lifecycle and renderer tests (33 cases), UI typecheck and Vite build passed. This is a **source-only accuracy fix**: no private package, game refusal, committed-export or installed-page retest was performed. At this version-gate stage, the existing vehicle reader still followed the third-party helper's selected-fill-type rule without proving positive litres in a unit; its “loaded spreaders” wording was not verified stock. A future accepted farm decision needs the same active version, a current period/temperature reading and either real owned organic stock or an owned spreader with a verified fill, with a game refusal comparison. No equipment or fertilizer was staged merely to populate the page.

**Fill-unit follow-up:** The local FS25 `FillUnit.lua` returns the live `spec_fillUnit.fillUnits` table, each unit has `fillType` and `fillLevel`, and the engine resets the type to `FillType.UNKNOWN` when level reaches zero. The third-party Restricted Periods helper checks a selected fill type but does not itself inspect litres. The current FarmHub page collector now requires a positive fill level in a matching LIQUIDMANURE, DIGESTATE or MANURE unit before counting an owned spreader as loaded; a positive fuel unit cannot make an empty organic unit count. If the fill-type manager is unavailable, vehicle totals are withheld instead of reported as zero. The UI also withholds vehicle totals on a truncated scan and says “Not read” rather than claiming no vehicles are loaded. Six focused suites (34 cases), UI typecheck and Vite build passed after this follow-up. This is still source-only: the loaded-vehicle list and game refusal have not been checked in a fresh game/export/installed-page comparison. No equipment was filled or placed to create a row.

Those choices are already available at the vehicle in game and a retained export can make their "current" state stale. V64 established only an empty applicable-vehicle state with StockGuard unchecked; it never accepted a nonempty reading. The dedicated collector/page and its presentation keys were removed under the farmer-value gate, while exact-mod detection remains in the catalog. The earlier source review and V64 evidence remain historical, not proof of a currently shipped dedicated page or actual autoload performance.

The same gate does **not** automatically exclude every implement control. Variable Working Depth's saved `isCalibrated` state can identify an owned implement needing calibration before fieldwork, a concrete preparation action; the setpoint is labelled as a control percentage, not measured soil depth. Its source-tested page remains for now, with nonempty installed validation still open. This distinction is based on the specific action each reading supports, not the presence of a settings field alone.

Smart Barrier's arm position and closing warning can help a farmer check access before routing a vehicle, so its owned-placeable reading remains. The previous labels said "now" even though V5 can display a held export. They now say "at last reading" and ask the reader to check the reading time before planning access. This wording correction is source/UI only; no new barrier movement, traffic or installed-page result is claimed.

This wording correction is source-only; the frozen 5.2.101 V84 installer still contains the earlier copy and its runtime result must be assessed against those exact bytes. A later private package/installed comparison is needed before attributing the correction to an installed build.

### Realistic Crop Rotation disease-state gap (14 November)

The exact reviewed `FS25_370461_Realistic_Crop_Rotation.zip` v1.1.0.1 source has a distinct disease system beyond the already accepted crop-plan rows. `RealisticCropRotationDisease:saveToXML` writes `realisticCropRotationDisease.xml` by farmland ID, including visible outbreak group/severity and pathogen reservoir load. At runtime `RealisticCropRotation.disease:getRisk` derives a **predictive pressure** for the standing crop from the reservoir/configuration without mutating it; `getRiskBand` maps that to 0-3, and `getWorstGroup` selects the worst **visible outbreak**. Those are different claims: pressure is a scouting priority, whereas a visible outbreak is an observed mod state. The game's disease/map UI already presents risk overlays, so the FarmHub reading compares **currently owned tracked parcels** for scouting from the last committed export, without prescribing chemicals. Disease records have no farm ID. The read-only collector now resolves current farmland ownership, caps scanned/returned rows, withholds counts when ownership or disease readings are incomplete, and requires the reviewed version and server state. The existing Realistic Crop Rotation page gains a distinct pressure-band/visible-outbreak card; its text calls pressure predictive and makes the export timestamp limit explicit. A focused Lua/merge test proves nonempty owned/foreign isolation and partial withholding; UI typecheck, Vite build and 27-locale verification passed. This is **source-tested only**. No actual nonempty disease game/export/installed-page comparison, other-farm multiplayer proof, infection progression or treatment outcome is established. The frozen V84 package predates this addition.

**AutoSwitch opening-hours join check and native Storage correction (14 November):** The exact v1.0.3.0 ZIP still hashes to `4BD4688F0D661D1A23AACFD179C850CC933155519AC47ABA3DCC979A1BFB1E17`. `OpeningHours.lua` keys overrides by `AS_Register.stationName`, which prefers `station.owningPlaceable:getName()` over `station.stationName`. Its `getStationHours` method **writes** a newly seen station to profile `horaires.xml`, so a read-only FarmHub collector must not call it. **AutoSwitch sale-register correction (14 November, source only):** Rechecking the exact AutoSwitch v1.0.3.0 ZIP SHA-256 `4BD4688F0D661D1A23AACFD179C850CC933155519AC47ABA3DCC979A1BFB1E17` against the local FS25 wiki and extracted `scripts/objects/SellingStation.lua` exposed a material mismatch. Base `SellingStation:sellFillType` returns the sale **price** (line 386) after `addFillLevelFromTool` passes positive moved litres into it (lines 317-57). AutoSwitch `scripts/Register.lua` lines 215-37 wraps `sellFillType`, assigns the super-call return to `moved`, then passes that return as **litres** to `AS_Register:addSale`; lines 162-89 store it and derive kilograms from it. The register's sale litres/kg are therefore not trustworthy on the reviewed base-game path. This is a third-party source finding; no actual sale or game log was measured, and other mod wrappers could change behavior. FarmHub now withholds this version's sale rows/counts/quantities from `autoSwitchRegister` rather than presenting price as volume. The page retains only farm-tagged weighbridge readings, which still require a nonempty game/export/installed-page test with AutoDrive Addon. **Soil Compaction incremental-reader feasibility (14 November, exact-source follow-up):** The reviewed `SoilCompaction.lua` exposes server object `g_soilCompaction`, `cells`, `keyToWorldCenter(key)` and `overlayRevision`. Normal compaction/relief writes call `markCellDirty` (incrementing the revision), daily weathering increments it after a chunk, and network metadata/cell replacements also mark it dirty. Local FS25 1.20 source confirms `FarmlandManager:getIsOwnedByFarmAtWorldPosition(farmId,x,z)` and `FSDensityMapUtil.getIsFieldAtWorldPos(x,z)` for a current owned-field-ground join. A resumable scan could therefore carry its `next` cursor across frames and restart/withhold results if the revision or grid table changes, avoiding a misleading mixed-time aggregate. The current `CompanionPages.collectEntry` invokes an entire page synchronously in `pcall`, however, and the mod's own overlay rebuild does a whole-grid scan only when the map opens because frequent full rescans stuttered. A useful FarmHub page still requires a separately budgeted incremental scanner, stable completion, bounded location grouping and source tests under a large changing grid. No partial-prefix result, map-wide count, collector or page was added from this research; no positive save fixture is presently identified.

**Native Storage buyer-price correction (14 November, source only):** The local FS25 1.20 `EconomyManager:getPricePerLiter` returns a seasonal base price for a fill type, not an offer from a selling place. The previous `StockDataCollector._attachSellPrices` seeded `bestSellPrice` with that number and `bestSellStation = "Market"`, so a farm with no eligible buyer, or one whose actual buyers paid less than the base, could receive a false actionable best-price label. Current source now sets `bestSellPrice` only from an eligible `SellingStation:getEffectiveFillTypePrice`, preserving farm-owner exclusion, fractional per-litre values and the owning-placeable name fallback. A focused production-Lua/consumer suite passed 22 cases, including no buyer, self-owned buyer, an actual buyer below the seasonal base, fractional prices and farm isolation. The frozen V5 5.2.106/exporter 5.1.0.93 V93R1 artifacts **predate** this correction; V93R1 cannot accept it. A newly packaged exporter, committed export and installed Storage comparison are still required. The app's separate economy/average-price fallback has not been reclassified by this source change; do not infer a real buyer from a base or average price.

**Storage buyer-price display priority (14 November, source only):** The NEW APP Storage consumer used to choose an economy crop location or XML average before the stock export's actual buyer price. Because the economy data can include a virtual `Market Base Prices` row, this could show a higher reference amount than the current eligible selling-station offer. `resolvePricePer1000` now prefers a positive stock `bestSellPrice` whose station is not the legacy `Market`/`Market Base Prices` sentinel, then falls back to the existing economy/reference path. The production Lua-to-consumer suite passed 22 cases, including an actual 0.80/L buyer against a 1.00/L virtual base, and NEW APP typecheck passed. This adjustment is later than the frozen V5 5.2.106 installer and V93R1 packet, so it has no installed acceptance. The economy fallback can still be an estimate or synthetic location; it must not be described as an observed buyer until its provenance is separated and the Storage page labels that distinction. No public artifact changed.

**Storage reference-price provenance (14 November, source only):** The NEW APP Storage row now records whether its price came from a named eligible stock selling-station offer or from economy crop locations/averages. The latter can include virtual `Market Base Prices` and inferred station/product pairs; the Storage price is visibly marked `estimate`, its hover says no current buyer offer was verified, and its Stations cell says no selling point available. A real buyer price still takes priority and keeps its name. The total is already titled `Estimated sell value`. The focused production Lua/consumer test passed 23 cases; NEW APP typecheck and i18n key/placeholder verification passed. New labels use English fallback in non-English locales pending translation. Frozen V5 5.2.106 and exporter 5.1.0.93 for V93R1 predate this source change and cannot accept it. Installed UI/game parity and the remaining economy source's synthetic station rows are separate follow-up gates; no public artifact changed.

**Economy station-offer source correction (14 November, source only):** Local FS25 1.20 `EconomyManager:getPricePerLiter(fillTypeIndex, useMultiplier)` supplies a season/difficulty adjusted fill-type base; its second parameter is a boolean multiplier switch, not a station. Actual `SellingStation:getEffectiveFillTypePrice` includes station-specific dynamics. The FarmHub Economy collector had been creating apparent offers from production input lists, product/name guesses, animal-dealer entries, hardcoded 0.80-0.95 multipliers and a hardcoded fill-type default-price table. Those paths could suggest a buyer and payout that the game never offered. Current source removes those synthesized station/product rows, uses only positive effective prices from a live accepted SellingStation for station quotes, omits empty nonbuyers, keeps the separately named Market Base Prices reference, and falls back to the owning placeable name if the engine station getter returns nil. This is deliberately a smaller set of quotes, not a claim that every game buying route has been discovered. The native environment suite passed 38 tests including no invented production/dealer offer, a real buyer below the seasonal base, and the engine-name fallback; the focused stock/Storage suite passed 23 tests. Classic app tests passed 157. **No private package, committed export, installed Economy-page test or same-time game Prices comparison includes this correction yet.** The Economy page still needs explicit reference-price presentation so a virtual base row is never mistaken for a buyer. V93R1 used older frozen bytes and does not validate this source change.
**Economy reference presentation correction (14 November, source only):** The NEW APP and classic Economy views previously mixed virtual `Market Base Prices` with named selling places: a base reference could be styled as the best buyer, included in the average of buyer offers, counted as a selling location, and trigger a false `Poor Market! Wait for better prices` warning. Current source moves named buyer offers before the base reference regardless of amount, leaves the reference visibly named with an explanation, shows `No selling point available` when no buyer is verified, computes the displayed average only from buyer rows, and excludes the virtual base from the by-location station list. A new truthful reference hint exists across all 27 locale files as English fallback; translated wording is pending. NEW APP typecheck and 27-locale placeholder/key verification passed; two rendered classic Economy cases passed for lower real buyer vs base and reference-only crop. The earlier production Lua tests passed. This page correction is **source tested only**; no installer, fresh game/export/installed-page comparison or public release includes it yet. The frozen V93R1 installer displayed the old logic.
